title: Learn Qur'anic Arabic
intro: For learners who can already read Arabic script. Arabic builds its words from three-letter roots poured into a small set of patterns; learn the patterns and you can work out words you've never seen. Every word here is a real word from the Qur'an — tap one to open its Bayan page.

levels.title: Reading the script
levels.summary: The letters, the vowel marks, and the special signs you only see in the Qur'an.
levels.note: Hidden for now: the course assumes learners can already read Arabic. Remove "hidden" to bring these lessons back.

levels.title: Roots and the فَعَلَ scale
levels.summary: Most words are three root letters poured into a pattern. Learn to find the root, read a pattern on the فَعَلَ scale, and work out what the commonest patterns mean.

levels.title: Pieces around the word
levels.summary: One Arabic word can hold three or four English words. Take a word apart: the joined particles وَ فَ بِ لِ كَ, the article, and the pronoun endings.

levels.title: Core vocabulary
levels.summary: The 300 most frequent words, in sets of ten. Together they make up three quarters of every word in the Qur'an.

levels.title: Verbs
levels.summary: Past and present, who is doing the action, commands, and what Forms II–X add to a root's meaning.

levels.title: Sentences
levels.summary: Sentences with and without a verb, إِنَّ and كَانَ, negation, questions, conditions and calling out with يَا.

levels.title: Reading real passages
levels.summary: Short sūrahs word by word — al-Fātiḥah, al-Ikhlāṣ, al-Falaq, an-Nās — then longer passages.

فَاعِل.role: the doer, one who does it

مَفْعُول.role: the done-to, what the action happens to

فَعُول.role: someone who does it a great deal

فَعَّال.role: someone who does it again and again

مَفْعَل.role: the place or time of the action

مَفْعِل.role: the place or time of the action

فُعُول.role: a plural, or the action itself
